tools.name: vinc_ingest
tools.summary: Write many nodes and edges in one call, merging by exact id. Search first (vinc_search) and reuse the ids you find; call vinc_conventions before your first write. Sending props replaces all stored props; use props_patch to change some. Skipped items are listed in warnings.
tools.reference: Merge an authored fragment of nodes and edges into this graph by exact id. The daily limit counts calls, not nodes, so send one piece of work in one call; reuse ids from vinc_search, and read vinc_conventions once per session first. For documents, follow the build-graph-from-documents prompt. Types record, concept, domain, bridge, episode and decision have their own tables; any other type becomes an open Entity listed in proposed_types. Edges: allowed pairs (concept and decision are interchangeable endpoints, except relates_to which stays concept→concept): supersedes = new→old of the same kind (record→record, decision→decision, concept:doc.*→concept:doc.*), with nonempty evidence; relates_to = concept→concept; prerequisite_of|derives_from|inherits_from = concept|decision → concept|decision; returns_to = distinct role concepts, with nonempty evidence; record → concept|decision for any of those four; connects_via = bridge → concept|decision; about = episode|decision → concept|decision; any-type = open-entity→open-entity (TYPED carrier). Invalid nodes and edges, and ids another account owns (`id_conflicts`), are skipped and reported in `warnings` with partial:true. Returns `stored`, each node as saved, to compare with what you sent. props replaces the whole object; props_patch with expected_rev merges. create_only:true and expected_rev guard against overwriting: a failed condition refuses the whole fragment with error:write_conflict and current_rev. Retry after a lost response: check vinc_operation_status, then resend identical arguments with the same operation_id; a repeat returns replayed:true.

params.description: When a record's claim became true, YYYY[-MM[-DD]]. This is a Record column: a Decision keeps its interval in props.valid_from and props.valid_until instead, and other kinds drop this field with a warning. An empty string clears it, and omitting it on a resend keeps the stored value. Set it when the record states the present state of the product, infrastructure or a process, because default reads return current claims only. Empty is allowed and reads as current, but a record with no start cannot later be retired cleanly.

params.name: nodes[].valid_until
params.description: When a record's claim stopped being true (half-open: it no longer holds at this instant), YYYY[-MM[-DD]]. Setting it retires the record without deleting it: resend just {id, type, valid_until}. An empty string clears it and the claim holds again. Once the date has passed, vinc_search and vinc_brief leave the claim out by default (counted in `validity_filtered`; historical:true or as_of brings it back); an empty valid_from never hides anything. It is not the only way to retire a claim: this field is a Record column, a Decision retires through props.valid_until, and a document through vinc_doc_put's valid_until. When a claim is superseded, set this on the old record to the new one's start date and keep the old record: it still describes what held then.
